programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: 100 years ago, land was stolen from the tribe of Ngati-Oneone in the East Coast of New Zealand. The land was taken from them to build a port, now known as, ‘Gisborne Port.’ After years of debating to give the land back and not being heard, the decedents of Rawiri Te Eketu o te Rangi have decided to march and take occupation over the land that is rightfully theirs. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: A proud son of Ngāti Manawa, war veteran Richard Dargaville, once a soldier for the New Zealand Army, he remains forever a soldier for te ao Māori. His service reflects not just commitment to a nation, but a deep dedication to whakapapa, identity, and the ongoing struggles and strengths of his whānau and wider Māori communities. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Through the act of karanga, we traverse both the physical and spiritual realms, guided by ancestral voices that echo through time. This sacred practice is far more than a ritual—it is a powerful form of cultural expression that binds the living with those who have passed on. Within the context of Whiria te hono, a distinguished collective of kaikaranga from Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei, the spiritual and practical responsibilities of this tradition are deeply honoured and carefully upheld. These wāhine carry the weight of generations with each call, embodying the values, stories, and mana of their iwi. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Charlie Rahiri describes himself as a reluctant iwi leader. But he was destined by his kaumātua to lead his iwi, Ngati Ranginui. He’s a direct descendant of Iwi chief Paraone Koikoi who surrendered his guns and pouches to the colonial office in 1864, only to be back in his kainga in Taumata three years later fighting for his land by pulling up survey pegs. We look at the changing role of a Māori Leader in Modern society through the eyes of Charlie Rahiri. (R)

programme.title: Compass
programme.sub-title: Labassa - If These Walls Could Talk
programme.desc: Compass was given rare access to Labassa, the historic Renaissance mansion in Melbourne to film many of the remaining tenants. We focus on the post war years of Jewish refugees and 1970's bohemians, artists and performers.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc: The Rev Kate Bottley explores the belief that laughter is a gift from God and meets clowns and comedians who explain how humour and joy profoundly connect them with their faith.

programme.title: ABC News At Noon

programme.title: Landline
programme.desc: A genetic insurance policy for cattle producers; Getting more value from plantation timber; The 'bee drover' sharing the highs and lows of the bee business; plus the monthly weather outlook.

programme.title: Gardening Australia
programme.desc: Costa and Sophie help residents of a holiday park with their gardens, Hannah meets volunteers helping gardeners to live independently, Sophie creates affordable containers, and we meet author and polio survivor Fran Henke.

programme.title: Recipe of the Year
programme.desc: From backyard get-togethers to milestone birthdays and everything in between, today our home cooks celebrate the recipes that bring people together.

programme.title: A Bite to Eat with Alice
programme.desc: Acting icon Rachel Ward joins Alice as they make a re-generative steak pie, while Rachel tries to move past her distaste for sauerkraut with Alice's help.

programme.title: Annabel Crabb's Civic Duty
programme.desc: In the early days, Parliament House hosted an all-male conclave of politicians and newspapermen, sharing a cramped environment and a complex code of conventions and mutual dependency. But the age of disruption has arrived.

programme.title: Joanna Lumley's Danube: Europe's Mightiest River
programme.desc: Join Joanna Lumley as she explores the pearl of the Danube Budapest by boat, rides the Children's Railway, discovers the city's Jewish heritage, meets Hungary's cowboys, and explores Dracula's Transylvania.

programme.title: Grand Designs New Zealand
programme.desc: An environmentally-committed young couple in Christchurch buck convention by going back to the future with a centuries-old building material.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Before the Accession, Fiona welcomes the Queen Consort and learns of her close ties to the Eden Project and The Big Lunch.

programme.title: The Forsytes
